# Authoring Test Contents

This document describe how to authorize test contents by computer literates who can operate a few simple programs and read the help content of various computing resources.

Each test content consists of SVG files of Ishihara plate and meta data defining the Graphic User Interface and the User Interaction.

## Preparation of SVG Files

### 38-plate created by Martin Krzywinski

As documented on [customized 38-plate](../svg_sources/README.md).

### Free ones

There are many SVG files free and in public domain in the Internet. 

### Generated by you
And for making your own Ishihara plates, [Ishihara Plate Generator](https://franciscouzo.github.io/ishihara/) is available.

## Content Structure

A test content file is JSON data with references to SVG files hosted locally or remotely.

**Hints:**
* The JSON data is governed by a JSON schema file. Therefore, with an advanced text editor like Visual Studio Code may horner the schema and provide syntax check and intellisense.

### Test Content

A test content is stored in a leaf folder containing:
* `plates.json` which conform to `"$schema": "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/zijianhuang/schemas/refs/heads/main/json/ColorBlindTestSchema.json"`.
* Optionally Ishihara plate svg files, while the SVG files can be stored outside folder SVG_Plates, and the relative paths could be like `"dir": "../../svg_sources/svglowrespng"` for local hosting.


### Initialization of Test Content

Rather than crafting plates.json from scratch, you may use a PowerShell script to scaffold then fine tune.
1. Copy all SVG files of the same test content to the test content leaf folder.
2. Run "InitPlatesJson.ps1" which initializes plates.json by scanning all svg file in the test content folder.

**Hints:**
1. Generally the plates in the same test content mandate similar GUI and UI, though this is not mandatory.
2. If you have prepare many test contents in leaf folders, `initAll.ps1` is for scanning all leaf folders and generate "plates.json" files accordingly.

After such initialization, you may fine-tune the JSON data. And obviously, in most cases you don't run those PS1 scripts again which will overwrite your changes.

### Provide Test Contents to App

The app will read `index.json` that aggregates the contents of all the `plates.json` files in the leaf folders. `GenerateColorBlindIndex.ps1` scans and generate `index.json`.
